question.stem:
A pharmacy administers influenza vaccine under a valid order and all personnel and product conditions are met. An employee interprets the policy's influenza exception to mandatory pre-administration MIIS review as permission not to report the dose.

How should this interpretation be corrected? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Require a new patient prescription solely to restore the reporting obligation.
Apply the exception only when the vaccine was paid for in cash.
Use a VAERS entry in place of the missing routine immunization report.
Report this dose even though the specified pre-administration query is excepted.

explanation.core_reasoning: 조회와 데이터 전송은 별도 행위다. 같은 시스템 이름 아래 있다는 이유로 한 예외를 다른 의무에 확대하지 않는다.

choice_analysis.A: 보고 의무가 새 처방을 받아야만 다시 생기는 구조가 아니다.
choice_analysis.B: 지급 방식으로 해당 MIIS 예외를 정한 규칙이 아니다.
choice_analysis.C: VAERS와 MIIS는 다른 목적·trigger의 시스템이다.
choice_analysis.D: Influenza/COVID의 지정 조회 예외가 MIIS 투약 기록 보고까지 면제하지 않는다.

explanation.learning_boundary: 한 판단을 위한 개별 작성 사례. 기존 원칙을 더 명확한 사례로 연습하며 새로운 법규 96개 또는 최근 기출의 재현이라는 뜻은 아닙니다.

question.stem:
A technician's vaccine-training file contains a six-hour ACPE course completed entirely through recorded modules. The technician also completed two documented hours of on-the-job training with an experienced certified immunizer and a skills checklist. The MOR is reviewing the initial education requirements for the DPH vaccine program.

What education deficiency remains? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: None; the six course hours and two on-the-job hours may be combined into an undifferentiated eight-hour total.
The on-the-job hours must be doubled, after which the recorded course can count as the required live component.
The ACPE course must satisfy the live-training requirement; the additional on-the-job training does not replace it.
One hour of annual immunization CE can replace the missing course component because that is the pharmacist standard.

explanation.core_reasoning: 기술직 초기 교육에서도 시간만 합산하지 않는다. 과정 내 live·실기 요건과 별도의 추가 OJT는 각각 확인해야 하며 한쪽을 마쳤다고 다른 쪽이 자동 충족되지 않는다.

choice_analysis.A: 정규 ACPE 과정의 구성과 추가 OJT는 구분된다. 총 8시간이라는 계산만으로 과정 내 최소 live training 요건이 충족되지 않는다.
choice_analysis.B: OJT를 더 하는 것으로 정규 과정 내 live training 요건을 대신할 수 없다. 두 요구는 정책에서 각각 정하고 있다.
choice_analysis.C: technician 과정은 최소 2시간의 live training과 연령에 맞는 IM·SC 실기평가 등을 포함해야 한다. 별도로 요구한 추가 OJT를 마쳤더라도 전부 녹화형인 과정의 결함은 남는다.
choice_analysis.D: pharmacist의 매년 1시간 CE는 technician의 초기 6시간 과정 구성 요건을 대체하지 않는다. 초기 교육과 유지 교육, 직종별 기준을 구분해야 한다.

explanation.learning_boundary: 기존 대표 문항을 별도 사례로 다시 작성했습니다. 원본과 새 문항의 풀이 기록은 각각 보존됩니다. 작성자 출처 대조와 편집 검토이며 독립 법규 감사 또는 실제 시험 난도 보정은 아닙니다.

question.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is revising the pickup procedure. One prescription is for an ordinary Schedule VI drug that has not been designated by the Commissioner for the additional-drug identification requirement. Another is for a drug that has received that formal designation. Which statements correctly describe the Customer Identifier rule? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The designated additional drug is within the Customer Identifier rule even though it is not described as a Schedule II through V drug.
Every Schedule VI dispensing is within the rule because Massachusetts calls Schedule VI a controlled-substance schedule.
Dispensing a controlled substance in Schedule II, III, IV, or V is within the rule's stated scope.
The ordinary Schedule VI drug is not brought within the rule merely by its Schedule VI classification.
A familiar customer may receive a covered drug without identification or the documented hardship procedure.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 9.04(14) applies the Customer Identifier requirement when a licensee dispenses a controlled substance in Schedules II through V or an additional drug formally designated under the cited Department regulation. It does not automatically cover every Massachusetts Schedule VI drug. A designated additional drug is covered by the designation, while an ordinary, undesignated Schedule VI drug is not covered merely because Massachusetts places prescription drugs in Schedule VI. Familiarity with the customer is not an independent exception.

choice_analysis.A: Correct: formal additional-drug designation is an independent route into the rule's scope.
choice_analysis.B: The regulation enumerates Schedules II through V and designated additional drugs, not Schedule VI as a whole.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: Schedule II through V dispensing is expressly within the rule.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: Schedule VI classification alone does not satisfy either enumerated route.
choice_analysis.E: Familiarity does not replace identification or, when serious hardship exists, the complete documentation, printed-information, and signature procedure.

related_facts: The Customer Identifier is obtained by inspecting valid government-issued identification of the ultimate user or agent
A serious-hardship dispensing requires both pharmacy documentation and recipient-entered identifying information and signature
explanation.mpje_trap: Massachusetts uses the term Schedule VI broadly, but this identification rule deliberately names Schedules II through V and a separate designation pathway.

question.stem: A Massachusetts collaborating pharmacist wants an appropriately trained certified technician to collect the vital signs contemplated by her collaborative practice agreement. The agreement says nothing at all about delegation. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Silence in the agreement operates as permission to delegate the duty.
Delegation is permitted because the technician is appropriately trained.
Delegation is permitted because collecting vital signs is not a dispensing act.
The agreement must specify which of the pharmacist's duties may be delegated.
The agreement must specify which duties under it may not be delegated.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 16.04(3) requires a collaborative practice agreement to specify those duties of the authorized pharmacist that MAY be delegated to other appropriately trained and authorized staff AND those duties under the agreement that SHALL NOT be delegated. An agreement that says nothing has not met either requirement, so there is no delegation power to exercise.

choice_analysis.A: The regulation requires affirmative specification, so silence is not permission.
choice_analysis.B: Training is necessary but does not supply the missing agreement terms.
choice_analysis.C: The nature of the task does not remove the requirement to specify.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: the delegable duties must be named.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: the non-delegable duties must also be named.

related_facts: Intern and technician support must still comply with 247 CMR 8.01 and 8.02 through 8.06
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates reason from the competence of the staff member rather than from the content of the agreement.

question.stem:
Case A: A pharmacist rejects a valid eligible prescription solely because it lacks the recommended words 'for pharmacist administration.'

Case B: A colleague treats the circular's example of quarterly prescriber reassessment as a mandatory new-prescription requirement exactly every 90 days for every product.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case B? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The reassessment example is not a universal exact 90-day new-prescription rule.
Signing a consent form replaces the circular's pre-administration counseling.
Because the notation is recommended, actual uncertainty about administration intent may be ignored.
The circular makes the recommended notation an absolute validity condition for every prescription.

explanation.core_reasoning: 권고 notation 누락 자체를 자동 무효 사유로 바꾸지 않는다. 필요한 의도 확인은 별개다. Appropriate interval과 예시를 고정 법정 validity로 혼동하지 않는다. 권고라는 이유로 실제 clinical·prescription uncertainty를 무시하지 않는다. Consent 기록과 실제 사전 상담은 다른 행동이다.

choice_analysis.A: 선택해야 하는 옳은 설명. Appropriate interval과 예시를 고정 법정 validity로 혼동하지 않는다.
choice_analysis.B:
선택하지 않아야 하는 잘못된 설명. Consent 기록과 실제 사전 상담은 다른 행동이다.
교정된 설명: Counseling is provided before administration and is not replaced by a consent signature.
choice_analysis.C:
선택하지 않아야 하는 잘못된 설명. 권고라는 이유로 실제 clinical·prescription uncertainty를 무시하지 않는다.
교정된 설명: A clinically meaningful uncertainty about intended administration should be clarified appropriately.
choice_analysis.D:
선택하지 않아야 하는 잘못된 설명. 권고 notation 누락 자체를 자동 무효 사유로 바꾸지 않는다. 필요한 의도 확인은 별개다.
교정된 설명: The absent recommended notation alone is not an automatic invalidity rule stated in the circular.

explanation.learning_boundary: 같은 family의 네 문항은 같은 두 사례와 네 판단을 공유하는 연습 변형이다. 독립적인 네 임상 사례로 세지 않는다.

question.stem:
Case A: A pharmacy replaces a required FDA Medication Guide with its software's generic consumer leaflet.

Case B: A staff member says that every product with a Medication Guide must also require enrollment in an active REMS program.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: A VIS is the same document as every prescription medicine's generic consumer leaflet.
A generic consumer leaflet is not automatically a substitute for the required FDA-approved Medication Guide.
Required information may also be needed at refills under the applicable Medication Guide rule.
The existence of a Medication Guide proves that REMS enrollment is required.

explanation.core_reasoning: CMI와 FDA-approved Medication Guide는 동일 문서가 아니다. Guide 존재와 active REMS의 구체적 요건을 별도로 확인한다. 해당 dispensing·refill의 Guide 제공 요건을 함께 확인한다. VIS·PPI·CMI·Medication Guide의 용도와 시점을 구별한다.

choice_analysis.A:
선택하지 않아야 하는 잘못된 설명. VIS·PPI·CMI·Medication Guide의 용도와 시점을 구별한다.
교정된 설명: A VIS is vaccine information supplied before vaccination, not a general prescription pickup leaflet.
choice_analysis.B: 선택해야 하는 옳은 설명. CMI와 FDA-approved Medication Guide는 동일 문서가 아니다.
choice_analysis.C: 선택해야 하는 옳은 설명. 해당 dispensing·refill의 Guide 제공 요건을 함께 확인한다.
choice_analysis.D:
선택하지 않아야 하는 잘못된 설명. Guide 존재와 active REMS의 구체적 요건을 별도로 확인한다.
교정된 설명: A Medication Guide requirement does not by itself prove a current REMS enrollment requirement.

explanation.learning_boundary: 같은 family의 네 문항은 같은 두 사례와 네 판단을 공유하는 연습 변형이다. 독립적인 네 임상 사례로 세지 않는다.

question.stem:
A pharmacy administers influenza vaccine under a valid order and all personnel and product conditions are met. An employee interprets the policy's influenza exception to mandatory pre-administration MIIS review as permission not to report the dose.

How should this interpretation be corrected? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Require a new patient prescription solely to restore the reporting obligation.
Apply the exception only when the vaccine was paid for in cash.
Use a VAERS entry in place of the missing routine immunization report.
Report this dose even though the specified pre-administration query is excepted.

explanation.core_reasoning: 조회와 데이터 전송은 별도 행위다. 같은 시스템 이름 아래 있다는 이유로 한 예외를 다른 의무에 확대하지 않는다.

choice_analysis.A: 보고 의무가 새 처방을 받아야만 다시 생기는 구조가 아니다.
choice_analysis.B: 지급 방식으로 해당 MIIS 예외를 정한 규칙이 아니다.
choice_analysis.C: VAERS와 MIIS는 다른 목적·trigger의 시스템이다.
choice_analysis.D: Influenza/COVID의 지정 조회 예외가 MIIS 투약 기록 보고까지 면제하지 않는다.

explanation.learning_boundary: 한 판단을 위한 개별 작성 사례. 기존 원칙을 더 명확한 사례로 연습하며 새로운 법규 96개 또는 최근 기출의 재현이라는 뜻은 아닙니다.

question.stem: A pharmacist compares Syndros oral solution with Marinol capsules. Which statements apply to Syndros? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Its Schedule II prescription may not be refilled.
The Massachusetts 30-day Schedule II validity period applies.
It follows the Schedule III refill rule used for Marinol.
The liquid dosage form makes it Schedule VI.
Syndros is Schedule II although Marinol capsules are Schedule III.

explanation.core_reasoning: The supported conclusions on these facts are: Its Schedule II prescription may not be refilled. The Massachusetts 30-day Schedule II validity period applies. Syndros is Schedule II although Marinol capsules are Schedule III.

choice_analysis.A: Supported: Its Schedule II prescription may not be refilled.
choice_analysis.B: Supported: The Massachusetts 30-day Schedule II validity period applies.
choice_analysis.C: Not supported: It follows the Schedule III refill rule used for Marinol.
choice_analysis.D: Not supported: The liquid dosage form makes it Schedule VI.
choice_analysis.E: Supported: Syndros is Schedule II although Marinol capsules are Schedule III.

related_facts: dronabinol oral solution (Syndros) is used for chemotherapy-associated nausea and vomiting and aids-related anorexia; it is federal Schedule II and Massachusetts Schedule II.
Federal law prohibits refilling a Schedule II prescription; additional dispensing requires a new lawful prescription or a permitted remainder of a partial fill.
A Massachusetts written or electronic Schedule II prescription becomes invalid 30 days after its issue date.
explanation.mpje_trap: Distinguish this near-miss from the controlling rule: 'It follows the Schedule III refill rule used for Marinol.'

question.stem: A Massachusetts prescriber writes for an eligible injectable to be administered in the pharmacy, specifying a single dose with three refills. The pharmacy manager says the refills make the prescription unusable for administration because the conditions require single doses. Who is right?

choices.text: The manager, because refills convert it into a course of therapy.
The manager, because each administration needs its own prescription.
The manager, unless the prescriber confirms the intent in writing.
The pharmacist, because single-dose prescribing may carry refills.
The pharmacist, because the single-dose condition governs packaging only.

explanation.core_reasoning: Among the conditions for dispensing by administration, the medication must be available in single-dose packaging AND prescribed in single doses, WITH OR WITHOUT REFILLS. The condition therefore controls how each dose is prescribed and packaged, and expressly tolerates refills, so a single dose with three refills satisfies it.

choice_analysis.A: The condition contemplates refills in terms.
choice_analysis.B: No rule requires a fresh prescription for each administration.
choice_analysis.C: No prescriber confirmation is required to cure a condition that is already met.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: the words with or without refills answer the point.
choice_analysis.E: The condition reaches both the packaging and the prescribing.

related_facts: Prescribers must reassess the patient and prescription at appropriate intervals
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates read single doses as excluding repetition and stop before the words that permit it.

question.stem:
Case A: A pharmacy replaces a required FDA Medication Guide with its software's generic consumer leaflet.

Case B: A staff member says that every product with a Medication Guide must also require enrollment in an active REMS program.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: A VIS is the same document as every prescription medicine's generic consumer leaflet.
A generic consumer leaflet is not automatically a substitute for the required FDA-approved Medication Guide.
Required information may also be needed at refills under the applicable Medication Guide rule.
The existence of a Medication Guide proves that REMS enrollment is required.

explanation.core_reasoning: CMI와 FDA-approved Medication Guide는 동일 문서가 아니다. Guide 존재와 active REMS의 구체적 요건을 별도로 확인한다. 해당 dispensing·refill의 Guide 제공 요건을 함께 확인한다. VIS·PPI·CMI·Medication Guide의 용도와 시점을 구별한다.

choice_analysis.A:
선택하지 않아야 하는 잘못된 설명. VIS·PPI·CMI·Medication Guide의 용도와 시점을 구별한다.
교정된 설명: A VIS is vaccine information supplied before vaccination, not a general prescription pickup leaflet.
choice_analysis.B: 선택해야 하는 옳은 설명. CMI와 FDA-approved Medication Guide는 동일 문서가 아니다.
choice_analysis.C: 선택해야 하는 옳은 설명. 해당 dispensing·refill의 Guide 제공 요건을 함께 확인한다.
choice_analysis.D:
선택하지 않아야 하는 잘못된 설명. Guide 존재와 active REMS의 구체적 요건을 별도로 확인한다.
교정된 설명: A Medication Guide requirement does not by itself prove a current REMS enrollment requirement.

explanation.learning_boundary: 같은 family의 네 문항은 같은 두 사례와 네 판단을 공유하는 연습 변형이다. 독립적인 네 임상 사례로 세지 않는다.

question.stem:
A pharmacy administers influenza vaccine under a valid order and all personnel and product conditions are met. An employee interprets the policy's influenza exception to mandatory pre-administration MIIS review as permission not to report the dose.

How should this interpretation be corrected? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Require a new patient prescription solely to restore the reporting obligation.
Apply the exception only when the vaccine was paid for in cash.
Use a VAERS entry in place of the missing routine immunization report.
Report this dose even though the specified pre-administration query is excepted.

explanation.core_reasoning: 조회와 데이터 전송은 별도 행위다. 같은 시스템 이름 아래 있다는 이유로 한 예외를 다른 의무에 확대하지 않는다.

choice_analysis.A: 보고 의무가 새 처방을 받아야만 다시 생기는 구조가 아니다.
choice_analysis.B: 지급 방식으로 해당 MIIS 예외를 정한 규칙이 아니다.
choice_analysis.C: VAERS와 MIIS는 다른 목적·trigger의 시스템이다.
choice_analysis.D: Influenza/COVID의 지정 조회 예외가 MIIS 투약 기록 보고까지 면제하지 않는다.

explanation.learning_boundary: 한 판단을 위한 개별 작성 사례. 기존 원칙을 더 명확한 사례로 연습하며 새로운 법규 96개 또는 최근 기출의 재현이라는 뜻은 아닙니다.

question.stem: A Massachusetts collaborating pharmacist wants an appropriately trained certified technician to collect the vital signs contemplated by her collaborative practice agreement. The agreement says nothing at all about delegation. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Silence in the agreement operates as permission to delegate the duty.
Delegation is permitted because the technician is appropriately trained.
Delegation is permitted because collecting vital signs is not a dispensing act.
The agreement must specify which of the pharmacist's duties may be delegated.
The agreement must specify which duties under it may not be delegated.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 16.04(3) requires a collaborative practice agreement to specify those duties of the authorized pharmacist that MAY be delegated to other appropriately trained and authorized staff AND those duties under the agreement that SHALL NOT be delegated. An agreement that says nothing has not met either requirement, so there is no delegation power to exercise.

choice_analysis.A: The regulation requires affirmative specification, so silence is not permission.
choice_analysis.B: Training is necessary but does not supply the missing agreement terms.
choice_analysis.C: The nature of the task does not remove the requirement to specify.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: the delegable duties must be named.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: the non-delegable duties must also be named.

related_facts: Intern and technician support must still comply with 247 CMR 8.01 and 8.02 through 8.06
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates reason from the competence of the staff member rather than from the content of the agreement.

question.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is revising the pickup procedure. One prescription is for an ordinary Schedule VI drug that has not been designated by the Commissioner for the additional-drug identification requirement. Another is for a drug that has received that formal designation. Which statements correctly describe the Customer Identifier rule? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The designated additional drug is within the Customer Identifier rule even though it is not described as a Schedule II through V drug.
Every Schedule VI dispensing is within the rule because Massachusetts calls Schedule VI a controlled-substance schedule.
Dispensing a controlled substance in Schedule II, III, IV, or V is within the rule's stated scope.
The ordinary Schedule VI drug is not brought within the rule merely by its Schedule VI classification.
A familiar customer may receive a covered drug without identification or the documented hardship procedure.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 9.04(14) applies the Customer Identifier requirement when a licensee dispenses a controlled substance in Schedules II through V or an additional drug formally designated under the cited Department regulation. It does not automatically cover every Massachusetts Schedule VI drug. A designated additional drug is covered by the designation, while an ordinary, undesignated Schedule VI drug is not covered merely because Massachusetts places prescription drugs in Schedule VI. Familiarity with the customer is not an independent exception.

choice_analysis.A: Correct: formal additional-drug designation is an independent route into the rule's scope.
choice_analysis.B: The regulation enumerates Schedules II through V and designated additional drugs, not Schedule VI as a whole.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: Schedule II through V dispensing is expressly within the rule.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: Schedule VI classification alone does not satisfy either enumerated route.
choice_analysis.E: Familiarity does not replace identification or, when serious hardship exists, the complete documentation, printed-information, and signature procedure.

related_facts: The Customer Identifier is obtained by inspecting valid government-issued identification of the ultimate user or agent
A serious-hardship dispensing requires both pharmacy documentation and recipient-entered identifying information and signature
explanation.mpje_trap: Massachusetts uses the term Schedule VI broadly, but this identification rule deliberately names Schedules II through V and a separate designation pathway.

question.stem: A Massachusetts collaborating pharmacist wants an appropriately trained certified technician to collect the vital signs contemplated by her collaborative practice agreement. The agreement says nothing at all about delegation. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Silence in the agreement operates as permission to delegate the duty.
Delegation is permitted because the technician is appropriately trained.
Delegation is permitted because collecting vital signs is not a dispensing act.
The agreement must specify which of the pharmacist's duties may be delegated.
The agreement must specify which duties under it may not be delegated.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 16.04(3) requires a collaborative practice agreement to specify those duties of the authorized pharmacist that MAY be delegated to other appropriately trained and authorized staff AND those duties under the agreement that SHALL NOT be delegated. An agreement that says nothing has not met either requirement, so there is no delegation power to exercise.

choice_analysis.A: The regulation requires affirmative specification, so silence is not permission.
choice_analysis.B: Training is necessary but does not supply the missing agreement terms.
choice_analysis.C: The nature of the task does not remove the requirement to specify.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: the delegable duties must be named.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: the non-delegable duties must also be named.

related_facts: Intern and technician support must still comply with 247 CMR 8.01 and 8.02 through 8.06
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates reason from the competence of the staff member rather than from the content of the agreement.

question.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is revising the pickup procedure. One prescription is for an ordinary Schedule VI drug that has not been designated by the Commissioner for the additional-drug identification requirement. Another is for a drug that has received that formal designation. Which statements correctly describe the Customer Identifier rule? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The designated additional drug is within the Customer Identifier rule even though it is not described as a Schedule II through V drug.
Every Schedule VI dispensing is within the rule because Massachusetts calls Schedule VI a controlled-substance schedule.
Dispensing a controlled substance in Schedule II, III, IV, or V is within the rule's stated scope.
The ordinary Schedule VI drug is not brought within the rule merely by its Schedule VI classification.
A familiar customer may receive a covered drug without identification or the documented hardship procedure.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 9.04(14) applies the Customer Identifier requirement when a licensee dispenses a controlled substance in Schedules II through V or an additional drug formally designated under the cited Department regulation. It does not automatically cover every Massachusetts Schedule VI drug. A designated additional drug is covered by the designation, while an ordinary, undesignated Schedule VI drug is not covered merely because Massachusetts places prescription drugs in Schedule VI. Familiarity with the customer is not an independent exception.

choice_analysis.A: Correct: formal additional-drug designation is an independent route into the rule's scope.
choice_analysis.B: The regulation enumerates Schedules II through V and designated additional drugs, not Schedule VI as a whole.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: Schedule II through V dispensing is expressly within the rule.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: Schedule VI classification alone does not satisfy either enumerated route.
choice_analysis.E: Familiarity does not replace identification or, when serious hardship exists, the complete documentation, printed-information, and signature procedure.

related_facts: The Customer Identifier is obtained by inspecting valid government-issued identification of the ultimate user or agent
A serious-hardship dispensing requires both pharmacy documentation and recipient-entered identifying information and signature
explanation.mpje_trap: Massachusetts uses the term Schedule VI broadly, but this identification rule deliberately names Schedules II through V and a separate designation pathway.

question.stem:
Case A: A pharmacist rejects a valid eligible prescription solely because it lacks the recommended words 'for pharmacist administration.'

Case B: A colleague treats the circular's example of quarterly prescriber reassessment as a mandatory new-prescription requirement exactly every 90 days for every product.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: Signing a consent form replaces the circular's pre-administration counseling.
The word 'quarterly' creates an exact 90-day new-prescription mandate for all eligible drugs.
A clinically meaningful uncertainty about intended administration should be clarified appropriately.
The absent recommended notation alone is not an automatic invalidity rule stated in the circular.

explanation.core_reasoning: 권고 notation 누락 자체를 자동 무효 사유로 바꾸지 않는다. 필요한 의도 확인은 별개다. Appropriate interval과 예시를 고정 법정 validity로 혼동하지 않는다. 권고라는 이유로 실제 clinical·prescription uncertainty를 무시하지 않는다. Consent 기록과 실제 사전 상담은 다른 행동이다.

choice_analysis.A:
선택하지 않아야 하는 잘못된 설명. Consent 기록과 실제 사전 상담은 다른 행동이다.
교정된 설명: Counseling is provided before administration and is not replaced by a consent signature.
choice_analysis.B:
선택하지 않아야 하는 잘못된 설명. Appropriate interval과 예시를 고정 법정 validity로 혼동하지 않는다.
교정된 설명: The reassessment example is not a universal exact 90-day new-prescription rule.
choice_analysis.C: 선택해야 하는 옳은 설명. 권고라는 이유로 실제 clinical·prescription uncertainty를 무시하지 않는다.
choice_analysis.D: 선택해야 하는 옳은 설명. 권고 notation 누락 자체를 자동 무효 사유로 바꾸지 않는다. 필요한 의도 확인은 별개다.

question.stem:
A pharmacy administers influenza vaccine under a valid order and all personnel and product conditions are met. An employee interprets the policy's influenza exception to mandatory pre-administration MIIS review as permission not to report the dose.

How should this interpretation be corrected? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Require a new patient prescription solely to restore the reporting obligation.
Apply the exception only when the vaccine was paid for in cash.
Use a VAERS entry in place of the missing routine immunization report.
Report this dose even though the specified pre-administration query is excepted.

explanation.core_reasoning: 조회와 데이터 전송은 별도 행위다. 같은 시스템 이름 아래 있다는 이유로 한 예외를 다른 의무에 확대하지 않는다.

choice_analysis.A: 보고 의무가 새 처방을 받아야만 다시 생기는 구조가 아니다.
choice_analysis.B: 지급 방식으로 해당 MIIS 예외를 정한 규칙이 아니다.
choice_analysis.C: VAERS와 MIIS는 다른 목적·trigger의 시스템이다.
choice_analysis.D: Influenza/COVID의 지정 조회 예외가 MIIS 투약 기록 보고까지 면제하지 않는다.

explanation.learning_boundary: 한 판단을 위한 개별 작성 사례. 기존 원칙을 더 명확한 사례로 연습하며 새로운 법규 96개 또는 최근 기출의 재현이라는 뜻은 아닙니다.
